newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares spent most of Thursday wavering between gains and losses, zig-zagging backwards and forwards over Wednesday's close for much of the day before settling slightly higher on balance.

Shares dropped quickly at the opening as buyers stood back from the market, still unnerved by gyrations in world markets after last week's comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan, which many saw as increasing the chances of a U.S. rate hike.
Weaker than expected U.S. November retail sales figures soothed some worries of a rate rise and the AEX left behind its 605.59 session low to close 0.85 points up at 611.41.
U.S. retail sales came in with a 0.4 percent fall in November, compared to an expected 0.3 percent rise, sending the U.S. 30-year treasury bond a point higher.
But dealers said any relief provided by the U.S. figures could be short-lived in a Dutch market spooked by its experiences since Greenspan's remarks.

"Normally you would call those figures from the U.S. very good but trading from now to the year end is going to be very nervous," a dealer said, adding he believed the market could get down to 590-600 in the near future before buyers re-emerged in any numbers. "We're still looking for the support level."

Analysts believe Greenspan's remarks, which warned of the potential damage to the economy arising from "irrational exuberance" in financial markets, made a tightening of monetary policy by the Fed more likely than not.

"When you look at corporate earnings growth and the AEX there's a big difference, that difference was made up by the fact that interest rates were coming down. If interest rates are going up then you have reason for a correction," said a dealer.
Another dealer said he believed the market was consolidating at a sensible pace and that the index would travel in a 602-620 range until the end of the year.
Philips stood out with a 1.20 guilder gain to 67.40, boosted by speculation it might be ready to sell its cable television activities, part of its loss making Media group.

The company responded to questions about a newspaper report that it wanted to shed the interests by saying it was weighing up non-performing interests as chairman Cor Boonstra had promised at the third quarter results news conference.

Elsewhere Royal Dutch was up 4.90 guilders on talk that it had been upgraded by a broker while Unilever fell 2.00 guilders to 284.60 and ING was unchanged at 57.50 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
